headline: Simulation ensembles reveal membrane-dependent conformations and protein self-assembly
label: Conformational Ensemble Modeling
summary: Four 2026 studies apply molecular dynamics to membrane-associated proteins, linking conformational ensembles to membrane binding and assembly.
synthesis: The common thread is simulation-derived conformational ensembles applied to proteins in membrane environments. The DspS study combines AlphaFold-Multimer, accelerated MD, and Markov state modeling to map CDA-dependent transmembrane helix dynamics in a full-length dimeric histidine kinase. The septin study uses all-atom MD of Cdc12 amphipathic helix pairs to show a bent, membrane-bound conformation and antiparallel salt-bridged cooperative binding. The hBD-3 study reports 57.0 μs of all-atom MD across monomers and dimers in model membranes and applies contact-matrix PCA/LDA to distinguish conformational states. The SARS-CoV-2 study shows, via MD and continuum modeling, that M protein self-interactions alone drive membrane clustering. What is new is the extension of ensemble analysis to membrane-embedded assemblies, where membrane association is central to the reported behavior. The items share a simulation-first approach but address distinct systems and do not establish a unified mechanism.
